name: Spring dash: a dash cancels a sideways spring's lock and holds the dot under a spike ceiling
techNote: A floor (top y 0, x -300-2000), a spring pointing right (the Course 5 ceiling spring's SpringScript: upForce 70, strength 300, movementLock 0.25; trigger 80x80 at x 60-140, y 0-80, turned -90 so transform.up is (1, 0)) and a spike ceiling (x 150-1000, y 120-152) over the launch. hitSpring starts the spring cutscene (cutsceneMode spring, the stick locked, Invoke cancelSpringCutscene 0.25 s) with momentum (4800, 175) and Velocity (0, 630): the launch rises into the ceiling and dies on tick 24. A dash pressed on the lock's first tick (the input's springDash 1, lockX 1) ends the cutscene (1236-1243) and dashes right level at y 49.2, under the spikes; the dot lands past x 570 and walks to the finish box (x 1050-1250, y 0-300). The spring's cancelSpringCutscene still fires 0.25 s after the hit, mid-dash (tick 30 here), and sets cutsceneMode none, so the dash's natural end (endDash with cutsceneMode no longer dash, 2028-2038) gives none of the stored 4689 back: a spring dash keeps its momentum only if something ends it before the lock would have (a second spring, spring-dash-stack).
